verdict.rationale: Airweave's own source connections sync apps, databases, and documents into searchable collections, including Airtable records and attachments and Bitbucket code files, so it goes well beyond chat transcripts. Business data and documents are clearly covered. However, ingesting raw JSON or uploading arbitrary documents directly, outside a connector, is not documented, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: explicit JSON/raw-payload ingestion, direct document upload API (non-connector), independent hands-on corroboration of ingestion breadth.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ingest documents, JSON, and business data into memory — not just chat transcripts

citations.quote: Airweave connects to your apps, databases, and documents, then turns them into knowledge you can search.
A source connection links a specific app or database to your collection. It handles authentication and automatically syncs data.
Airtable source connector — syncs bases, tables, records, comments, attachments.
It supports syncing workspaces, repositories, directories, and code files with configurable filtering options for branches and file types.
Airweave looks like it copies the data and has a RAG that is processing your queries
